look_here_first: Start with 2 distinct PETIOLE nectar glands and BROAD sharply toothed/serrated 3(–5)-lobed leaf; compare smooth edged narrow 3–9-lobed P. tenuiloba. Then check large purplish flower with layered corona and a fat maypop 30–60 mm, much larger than the little dark berries of green-flowered relatives.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: vigorous perennial climbing or trailing vine with axillary tendrils

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: two conspicuous sessile extrafloral nectary glands on the petiole

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lobes broad, pointed, and distinctly serrate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: large solitary flower with purple-and-white multi-whorled corona

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: large ovoid to subglobose maypop fruit

lookalikes.differences: Separate from P. lutea by petiole glands, serrated broad lobes, and huge flowers; separate from P. tenuiloba by the broad serrated lobes and large showy flower.
